core.title: Compose every flow router into a journey
core.given: A plan artifact that declares one or more flow routers (regardless of what was edited).
core.when: The plan artifact is validated at CONFIRM, where any finding of this rule blocks CONFIRM (confirm-blocking).
core.then: Declare at least one journey and make every flow router composed into a journey: each flow router is a journey's entrypoint flow router, or the destination of a continuation reachable from a journey's entrypoint.
prefer: For each flow router, state the journey that starts it (what triggers the routing decision) or the continuation that leads into it from a reachable flow router.
Decide the end-to-end flow: for each flow router, state what happens after its user/system flow completes via continuations.
avoid: Stopping the decomposition at flow routers so it looks complete while the end-to-end flow was never decided.
A plan with flow routers and no journey (vacuous topology), relying on the continuation-closure rule passing vacuously.
Orphan flow routers: routing decisions with no stated trigger and no stated place in the product flow.
core.why: The journey is where the plan says what starts a routing decision and what happens after its user/system flow completes. The sibling continuation-closure rule only validates the journeys a plan declares, so plans with none, or with flow routers outside every journey, would pass it vacuously; this rule closes that gap.
evidence: The journey-composition check reports no findings at CONFIRM; enforcement is confirm-blocking, so any finding blocks CONFIRM.

Each finding identifies the uncomposed flow router, the number of journeys the plan declares, and the reason, so it is visible which flow router is uncomposed and whether the plan declares zero journeys.
verification: Static plan-graph reachability check (closure of the plan's route space): for every declared flow router, verify it is composed — the entrypoint of at least one journey, or the destination of a continuation reachable from a journey's entrypoint. The subject of the check is the flow router; findings are reported per uncomposed flow router.
Vacuous topology: a plan that declares flow routers but no journey has no composed flow router, so every flow router is reported.
Enforcement: confirm-blocking — findings of this rule block CONFIRM.
Severity 4; disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

Scope boundary: the check covers only journey composition. Whether the declared journeys' continuations are themselves closed is the sibling continuation-closure rule, not this check; this rule exists precisely to close that rule's vacuous-pass gap (plans with no journeys, or flow routers outside every journey).

fires: At CONFIRM, a plan artifact declares flow routers but declares no journey (vacuous topology): every flow router is reported.
At CONFIRM, a plan artifact declares journeys, but a flow router is neither a journey entrypoint nor the destination of any continuation reachable from one.
At CONFIRM, a plan artifact whose only change is adding a flow router, or one that was not edited at all but already leaves a flow router outside every journey (non-exhaustive examples).
At CONFIRM, after a journey entrypoint is retargeted, a continuation endpoint is changed, or a continuation or journey is removed, so a flow router is no longer reached (non-exhaustive examples).
doesNotFire: A plan artifact that declares no flow routers at all.
Checking whether declared journeys' continuations are themselves closed (that is the sibling continuation-closure rule, not this one).

neutralityNotes: This is a plan-artifact content rule, so almost everything is already stack-neutral; the ATDD planner vocabulary it relies on (journey, flow router, continuation, user/system flow, CONFIRM phase) is methodology-level and kept verbatim — journeys are already a vocabulary artifact (urn.journey), and task terms belong to the rule, not the profile. Only the validator/implementation id, the validation-catalog ids (family/template/variant/subject_kind) and the finding-field schema are Bun realization details (bunOnly). bun.json declares no plan-root, plan-suffix or plan-declaration values, so the single profile requirement is the plan-artifact kind mapping (ATDD-Bun: 'plan'). Severity 4 and strict disposition stay in core:verification per the not-profile-keys rule; the severity number is on the shared ATDD severity scale and is not stack-specific.
